questions.prompt: A PreToolUse command hook finds a forbidden command. Which behaviour blocks the call and tells Claude why?
questions.explain: Exit code 2 blocks the tool call, and the stderr text is what Claude sees as the reason. Exit 0 means no decision and exit 1 is a non-blocking error.

options.text: Write the reason to stderr and exit with code 2
Write the reason to stdout and exit with code 1
options.misconception: Exit 1 is a non-blocking error: the action proceeds.

options.text: Write the reason to stderr and exit with code 0
options.misconception: Exit 0 means no decision. The normal permission flow still applies.

options.text: Add a line to the instructions file asking Claude to stop
options.misconception: Instructions influence the model, and the tool call goes ahead unless something enforces a stop.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a blocking PreToolUse hook in order.
questions.explain: Each step needs the one before: the call must be requested before the event exists, the hook can only test what it has been sent, and the refusal and reason follow from the exit.
items: Claude asks to run a Bash command
The harness sends the event as JSON to the hook
The script reads tool_input.command and tests it
On a match it prints a reason to stderr and exits 2
The call is refused and Claude sees the reason

why.Claude asks to run a Bash command: Nothing exists to check until Claude requests a tool call.
why.The harness sends the event as JSON to t: The hook can only decide after the harness hands it the event on stdin.
why.The script reads tool_input.command and: The script can only test the command once it has the JSON.
why.On a match it prints a reason to stderr: Exit 2 with a stderr reason is only produced after the test matches.
why.The call is refused and Claude sees the: The reason is shown to Claude only once the hook has blocked the call.

questions.prompt: Your guard script has a typo and crashes with exit code 1 and no JSON output. What happens to the command it was meant to check?
questions.explain: Any exit code other than 2, with no valid JSON, is a non-blocking error on most events, so the action proceeds. The guard fails open unless configured to block on failure.

options.text: The hook does not block it
It is blocked, because a failing guard stops everything
options.misconception: Exit 2 blocks, and a crash leaves the action to proceed.

options.text: It is held until you answer a prompt about the crash
options.misconception: The action proceeds on most events, and no prompt about the crash appears.

options.text: It runs in the sandbox instead of normally
options.misconception: The docs describe no sandbox fallback for hooks. They say the action proceeds.

questions.prompt: A colleague describes what their grep hook protects. Which line overclaims?
questions.explain: A hook that greps the command text sees only that text. A differently spelled or script-hidden command passes it, and a sandbox is a separate control.

lines.text: It runs before the Bash tool and can refuse the call
lines.why: A PreToolUse hook fires before the tool runs.

lines.text: It cannot see files added with an @ reference in the prompt
lines.why: No tool call happens, so no hook fires.

lines.text: Because it blocks 'drop table', no database can ever be dropped
It runs with my user permissions, so I reviewed it first
lines.why: Command hooks run with your full user permissions.

questions.prompt: In an unfamiliar repository, sort each item: can it run as you, or does it only steer the model?
bins: Code that can run as you
Text that only steers the model
questions.explain: Command hooks execute with your privileges, as does a script they call. An instructions file is read into context.

items.bin: Code that can run as you
items.misconception: Command hooks execute shell commands with your user permissions.

items.text: A CLAUDE.md paragraph asking for care with deletes
items.bin: Text that only steers the model
items.misconception: Instructions are text in the context. They influence the model but execute nothing.

items.text: The shell script a hook points at
items.bin: Code that can run as you
items.misconception: The script is the hook. It runs as you whatever its name suggests.

questions.prompt: An agent will place orders with a vendor of custom DNA. What is the best safeguard?
questions.explain: Put one checkpoint in the path that can refuse dual-use orders. A line in the brief can be one layer, and it cannot be the only one.

options.text: Route every order through one screening checkpoint that can refuse
Rely only on a line in the brief telling the agent to decline risky orders
options.misconception: A brief is advice, and the agent may not recognise a risky order. A checkpoint in the path is needed as well.

options.text: Read a weekly summary of the orders after they have already been placed
options.misconception: A review after the fact cannot stop an order that has already gone out.

options.text: Skip screening, because the order account belongs to your own lab group
options.misconception: Whose account it is does not change what the order can do.
